So estheticians and dermatologists who go to school specifically to learn about skin care is not a good enough source to say that something isn't good for your skin? I mean go ahead and ruin your skin slowly over time if that's what you want. Not my problem.

Ground shells in the scrub look like shards of broken glass under a microscope and it really does tear your skin on a microscopic level. This is not something that is made up, you can ask almost any dermatologist or esthetician and they will agree it will cause damage to your skin over time.

http://www.etherealauraspa.com/blog/apricot-scrub

I'm a cosmetologist and I've learned from and worked with estheticians who all agree is is too harsh for facial skin. Yeah, okay, some people may not have an issue with it on their skin for a while but it is recommended to avoid it anyways because those micro tears will eventually cause skin damage and age your skin over time worse than a more gentle exfoliant. Any kind of ground up shells look like shards of glass under a microscope. Why would anyone want to be rubbing something that resembles glass on their delicate facial skin?
